note: Adapted from Hill (1927), Memoirs of the National Museum, Melbourne 7; the original combination is Microcerotermes nervosus, n. sp. The measurement table is damaged in the OCR and is not transcribed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is very close to M. parviceps but smaller and paler, with distinctly smaller and paler wings bearing smaller and fewer micrasters; it differs from M. serratus, which is hairier, darker, with darker, longer and relatively narrower wings and a differently shaped pronotum. The soldier resembles M. newmani but is larger, with a differently shaped head, mandibles and gula; Holmgren noted that the soldier of M. papuanus has a broader, wholly hairy head, while its alate is darker, hairier and slightly larger.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head uniform Sandford brown; mandibles nearly black; thorax, legs and antennae clay colour. Head very long and narrow, parallel-sided, scarcely narrowed to the mandibular articulation; mandibles short and moderately stout, slightly curved, finely serrate, with a small distinct tooth at the proximal third, sometimes hidden by the labrum; labrum short and wide, parallel-sided, bluntly pointed, with ten setae arranged in pairs; gula long and narrow, its narrowest part one-fifth the width of the head; antennae 13-jointed, longer than the mandibles.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large form: head and postclypeus ochraceous orange, the postclypeus with a large dark ferruginous area at the mandibular articulation; anteclypeus hyaline; labrum light orange yellow; antennae, thorax and legs cream buff. Small form paler, the frons white. Head nearly parallel-sided, broadly rounded behind; postclypeus strongly convex, hemispherical behind and truncate in front, with a distinct ferruginous median suture; antennae 13-jointed, the 3rd joint shortest, the 4th to 8th moniliform, the 9th to 12th turbinate, the 12th noticeably longer than the 11th but shorter than the 13th.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Chestnut, the head a little darker than the pronotum and abdomen; postclypeus tawny olive; antennae, mouth parts and legs clay colour; pleura and sternites suffused with brown; wings light fuscous. Very similar to M. parviceps but smaller and paler; eyes small, circular and prominent; ocelli very small, separated from the eyes by about their long diameter; antennae 14-jointed, the joints short and wide, the 14th as wide as the 13th; wings distinctly smaller and paler than in M. parviceps, the micrasters smaller and fewer; legs short and stout, tibial spurs 3:2:2, claws short and stout.
